parts.note: read straight, urgent tasks; read with the question mark, the jobs of a valet who irons (presses) clothes

explanation.surface: A list of the most urgent jobs awaiting a gentleman's manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties that are pressing are urgent tasks, and a valet's duties include pressing his master's clothes.

clue.text: The craftsman to occupy himself in casual fashion

definitions.meaning: a maker of pots and ceramics

definitions.text: to occupy himself in casual fashion
definitions.meaning: to pass time ... about, doing small jobs idly

explanation.surface: A craftsman fills his time in a relaxed, unhurried way.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramicist is a potter, and to potter is to busy oneself idly with trifles.

clue.text: A way out for a coloured lady who has lost her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the first letter of the lady's word is cut off

parts.note: an old, now offensive, term for a black woman, a NEGRESS

explanation.surface: An exit is offered to a woman who has lost her composure.
explanation.walkthrough: The dated term NEGRESS (now offensive) loses its head N, leaving the exit word.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit or means of leaving a place, a formal synonym for a way out.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is the single word 'Upset' (6) for SADDEN: a bare definition with no wordplay or second definition; likely cut short in the OCR, and no scan is available.

clue.text: Publicity means to make west relent

indicators.note: the words west and relent are used as raw material to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advertising is a way to persuade the West to soften its stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsletter is a regular bulletin sent out to inform and publicise, so a means of publicity.

clue.text: Such a heave puts Ruth in confusion

indicators.note: being in confusion signals that the letters of puts and Ruth are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A big push throws a woman called Ruth into disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: An upthrust is an upward push or heave, as of rock strata or a buoyant force.

clue.text: Vaguely allusive to content of a melody

definitions.meaning: hinted at but uncertain, rumoured, not yet settled
what is contained in a tune, an air, is literally inside that air

explanation.surface: Something hinted at only vaguely, like the words carried by a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour that is in the air is felt vaguely around, and an air is a melody whose contents lie within it.

indicators.note: putting things in disorder means the letters of set and daily are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something fixed each day becomes chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something steadily means doing it at an even, regular pace, so the two adverbs are synonyms.

definitions.meaning: to refuse or reject an offer
to turn off into a side road, turning down a street

explanation.surface: Refusing to alter one's course.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to decline it, and turning down a lane alters one's route.

indicators.note: organising the letters of astute means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A leading personality gained through shrewd management.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure standing out from its plinth, punning on a prominent person.

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of Yes and later are altered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to a wind of change, but only later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind of change' is a famous political phrase; 'of' is a link and 'change' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a breeze blowing from the east, a type of wind named by direction.

definitions.meaning: a member of the Religious Society of ...
a pal or mate

explanation.surface: A Quaker who is also a good companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, and a friend is a companion.

clue.text: Double blow — a once-popular prelude to "Who's there?"

indicators.note: double means the word for a blow is written twice in a row

parts.note: a knock is a blow or rap

explanation.surface: Two raps on the door begin the old joke ritual of asking who is there.
explanation.walkthrough: The once-popular joke format opens with the phrase answered by "Who's there?".
explanation.definitionFit: Knock-knock jokes begin with this call, to which the listener replies with the stock question about who is there.

clue.text: Does not sit until stoppage is complete

parts.note: one who does not sit stands
till is a synonym of until

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to sit down until the work stoppage is total.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a complete halt, a stoppage in which nothing moves at all.

definitions.meaning: one who springs or leaps
a ... spaniel, a gundog breed

explanation.surface: A sweater bought for a pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is something that leaps, and the springer spaniel is a well-known dog breed.

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is left out of the word for dying

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A celebrated soldier dies without a single companion.
explanation.walkthrough: John J. Pershing commanded the American forces in France in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: General John J. Pershing led the American Expeditionary Forces in 1917-18, a famous military man.

definitions.meaning: an official ... manages the affairs of a bankrupt
a radio set picks up broadcasts

explanation.surface: An official radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an official receiver is appointed to wind up a bankrupt's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver is an appointed officer in bankruptcy and also an apparatus that picks up radio signals.

parts.note: Peter's head, its first letter, is P; Peterhead is also a Scottish port
an allusion is a reference to something

explanation.surface: A fine allusion to the Scottish port of Peterhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhead is a fishing town in north-east Scotland; split as Peter + head it gives the first letter of Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option one favours, so it is a choice.

parts.note: to issue cards is to deal them out

explanation.surface: A harsh trial or some problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience, a severe test of endurance.

definitions.meaning: a slow, stately ballroom dance in triple time
a piece composed in that rhythm

explanation.surface: Music for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a courtly dance in three-four time and also a piece of music written for it.

clue.text: Like a bird, to the rear

explanation.surface: Positioned behind, as a bird might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning behind or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: Part of the foot marching soldiers must keep properly

definitions.meaning: the arched middle of the foot
soldiers on parade must keep in time with one another

explanation.surface: Soldiers on the march must look after their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arch of the foot, and marching troops keep in step together.

clue.text: Reefs produced risks ere found out

indicators.note: found out here means the letters of risks and ere are rearranged, sorted out of order

explanation.surface: Rocks at sea revealed dangers that were discovered too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Skerries are small rocky islets or reefs, a word used especially around Scottish coasts.

definitions.meaning: to feel sorrow for a loss
in Scotland a ... is a farm overseer or steward

explanation.surface: Lamenting the loss of a governor.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIEVE is the Scots word for a farm manager or bailiff.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to mourn, and a grieve is a Scottish farm overseer, one who governs the farm.

clue.text: Political policy henpecked husband longs for

definitions.meaning: self-government, as sought for Ireland
a man dominated by his wife wishes to be in charge in his own house

explanation.surface: A downtrodden husband dreams of political independence.
explanation.walkthrough: Home Rule was the campaign for Irish self-government; a henpecked man wants rule at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Home Rule was the policy of self-government for Ireland, and it also means being master in one's household.

definitions.meaning: to look at or pay attention
to hold in respect

explanation.surface: An announcement of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to notice or look at it, and to hold someone in regard is to esteem them.

definitions.meaning: minimal, as in a ... staff
the bony framework of the body

explanation.surface: Bones stripped bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton crew is a minimal, bare one, and the skeleton is the body's framework of bones.
